content:
Give your church a way to receive mail, answer calls and share working documents. USPS offers mailboxes, and office services can provide phone and collaboration tools across the devices your team uses.

If you work from home, use the same workstation and information-security checks you would use for an office elsewhere. The OSHA and FTC guidance below provides practical starting points for arranging your work and protecting the information you handle.

---

## Choose a mailing address

A USPS PO Box holds mail at a Post Office until you collect it. It can help keep your home address private. Compare locations, box sizes and access hours against your mail volume and pickup schedule.

A private mailbox is a different arrangement. USPS calls businesses that receive mail for customers commercial mail receiving agencies, or CMRAs. They hold mail for pickup or remail it with new postage. If you are considering a virtual mailbox, ask the provider how it handles physical mail and digital delivery.

USPS rules cover mail received through an agency, including PS Form 1583, Application for Delivery of Mail Through Agent. Ask the provider to explain its application and identity-verification process before you subscribe.

<Callout type="warning">
USPS Street Addressing can support private-carrier deliveries at participating PO Box locations, subject to restrictions. Its agreement prohibits using that address as your physical residence or place of business in legal documents. Keep that limitation in view when completing forms.
</Callout>

---

## Arrange mailbox access and pickup

To reserve a USPS PO Box online, select the location, size and payment period, then complete the application and payment. Bring the printed application and two acceptable forms of identification to that Post Office within 30 days of submitting the online application.

PS Form 1093 explains the identification requirements, including current photo identification and proof of your physical address. Check the acceptable documents before making the trip.

USPS encourages you to empty the box regularly and keep application information current. Check the location's lobby and counter hours, including how to collect packages that do not fit in the box. Confirm which people may collect your church's mail.

<Callout type="important">
Postal procedures and product features were checked on October 16, 2026. Before paying, confirm current fees, renewal terms, identification requirements and available services with USPS or your chosen provider. Confirm phone and productivity-plan features with the vendors too.
</Callout>

---

## Arrange your home workstation

Use OSHA's workstation evaluation checklist to review the place where you will do church administration. Treat it as practical setup guidance rather than a determination of your church's legal obligations.

Check that your back has support and your feet rest on the floor or a stable footrest. Position the mouse beside the keyboard so you can use it without reaching. Adjust the screen so you can read it without bending your neck or leaning forward.

If you use the phone while typing, consider a headset that lets you keep your head upright and shoulders relaxed. Review the arrangement while doing your actual computer and phone work.

---

## Evaluate equipment before acquiring it

Use OSHA's purchasing checklist when considering a desk, chair, monitor or laptop accessories. Check screen visibility and adjustability, space for your keyboard and mouse, and room for your legs under the desk.

OSHA recommends an external keyboard and pointing device for laptops and tablets. Its guide also suggests trying a chair for comfort and fit before purchasing it. Apply those fit checks to equipment you are offered as well as equipment you might buy.

<Callout type="tip">
Check the workstation before deciding which item to acquire. OSHA provides both an evaluation checklist for the setup and a purchasing checklist for equipment. Use the evaluation to identify what needs attention.
</Callout>

---

## Set up a church phone number

Compare a phone service's calling devices and administrative controls. For example, Google Voice supports mobile devices, laptops and supported desk phones. Its managed service offers number assignment and porting, with call-routing features depending on the plan.

Ask whether the plan includes the routing your church needs, such as a ring group or automated attendant. Check the selected edition rather than assuming every feature on a vendor's product page comes with every subscription.

Before sharing the number, make a test call and check the configured routing and voicemail. Use the provider's administrative tools to assign the number to the intended user.

Read the emergency-calling instructions separately. Google says Voice emergency calling is unavailable during a power outage, lost internet connection or Voice service outage, and directs users to an alternative phone service. Include that limitation when explaining the phone setup to your team.

---

## Choose everyday productivity tools

Compare the tools for email, documents, spreadsheets, file sharing and calendars. Google's Workspace nonprofit offering, for example, lists Gmail, Docs, Sheets, Drive and Calendar, with email at your own domain. Confirm eligibility and the features of the edition you are considering.

For shared administration, Google allows administrator roles with different privileges. Assign a role according to the tasks a person will manage, such as users or service settings. Keep broad administrative access limited to people responsible for that work, following the FTC's access-control advice.

Use individual user accounts to control access to information. The FTC recommends considering separate accounts rather than giving everyone unrestricted access to stored personal data.

---

## Protect paper and shared files

Use the FTC's information-security guidance to review what you collect and who can access it. Limit access to the information people need for their responsibilities. Store sensitive paper records and removable media in a locked room or cabinet, and control access to the keys.

For team documents, check ownership as well as sharing. Google distinguishes shared drives, whose files belong to the organization, from an individual's My Drive. Files in a shared drive remain when a member leaves and an administrator deletes that person's account.

Check the sharing settings before putting sensitive documents into a team drive. Google notes that shared-drive members generally see the same content, with limited-access folders available to restrict access. Choose the applicable permissions rather than assuming every office helper should see every file.

---

## Check the setup with your team

Use this final checklist to revisit the services and controls you selected:

- [ ] Confirm mailbox pickup arrangements and current application information.
- [ ] Review the workstation with OSHA's evaluation checklist.
- [ ] Test the phone number's routing and voicemail.
- [ ] Explain the phone provider's emergency-calling limitations.
- [ ] Assign administrative roles according to responsibilities.
- [ ] Check shared-file ownership, permissions and sensitive-paper storage.

<Callout type="scripture">
*"Whatever you do, do your work heartily, as for the Lord rather than for men,"* — Colossians 3:23 (LSB)
</Callout>
excerpt: Set up your church’s mailing address, home workstation, phone service and shared office tools, with checks for access and sensitive information.
title: Setting Up the Church Office

sources.claim: Opening and mailing-address section: PO Box mail storage, privacy, location/size/hours checks; online reservation, payment, two IDs and within 30 days; private-carrier service subject to availability; package collection. Mailbox and final checklist steps apply these documented features. Confirm current local services and prices.
sources.quote: 2 forms of acceptable U.S. identification (within 30 days of submitting your online application).

sources.claim: Mailbox operations: current photo and non-photo address identification, emptying box regularly, current application information. Pickup checks and final checklist apply the form instructions. No renewal deadline is asserted because older form and public page describe timing differently.
sources.quote:
The information on your PS Form 1093 must always be current.
We encourage you to empty your box regularly.

sources.claim: Street Addressing warning: prohibition on using the PO Box street address as physical residence or business address in legal documents.
sources.quote: You may not use the PO Box “street address” option as your physical residence or place of business in Legal documents.

sources.claim: Private mailbox section: CMRA definition, pickup or remailing with new postage, PS Form 1583 customer application and identity verification. Digital-delivery question reflects 1.8.4(2), which mentions email if correspondence is scanned. No scanning feature or price is promised.
sources.quote: The CMRA accepts delivery of the mail and holds it for pickup or remails it to the addressee, prepaid with new postage.

sources.claim: Opening home-office advice; workstation section and final checklist: evaluation is guidance; back and foot support, mouse placement, readable monitor positioning, headset for phone/computer work. Equipment tip applies the paired checklists.
sources.quote: This checklist can help you create a safe and comfortable computer workstation.

sources.claim: Equipment section and tip: purchasing checklist covers monitor size/adjustability, desk and leg space, external laptop keyboard/input device and trying chair for comfort and fit. Applying checks to offered equipment is an organizing suggestion.
sources.quote: Provide an external keyboard and input device for laptops and tablets.

sources.claim: Phone section and opening: Voice supports mobile/laptop/supported desk devices, admin number assignment/porting and plan-dependent ring groups/auto attendants; suggested routing/voicemail test checks these features. Confirm edition before subscribing.
sources.quote:
Your Voice line works on mobile devices, laptops, and supported desk phones
number assignment, number porting, and billing

sources.claim: Phone emergency paragraph and final checklist: Google outage limitations and instruction to use an alternative phone service; practical team explanation applies vendor instruction. No universal emergency-call support claim.
sources.quote: emergency calling will not be available on Google Voice. Use an alternative phone service to dial emergency services instead.

sources.claim: Productivity section: Workspace nonprofit offering includes custom-domain email and listed apps. Comparison and eligibility/edition checks are suggested use of vendor information, not a guarantee of church eligibility, prices or quotas.
sources.quote: All Google Workspace plans provide a custom email for your nonprofit and include collaboration tools like Gmail, Calendar, Meet, Chat, Drive, Docs, Sheets

sources.claim: Productivity and final checklist: Google permits sharing administrative responsibilities through roles; assign privileges according to actual management duties.
sources.quote: You can share the responsibility of managing your Google Workspace or Cloud Identity account by assigning administrator roles to other users.

sources.claim: Opening, productivity and files: FTC practical security starting point, separate user accounts and need-to-know permissions, limited administrative access; no assertion of church-specific statutory coverage.
sources.quote: For your network, consider steps such as separate user accounts to limit access to the places where personal data is stored

sources.claim: Files and final checklist: restrict sensitive paper and media to locked storage and control keys, with job-based access. Practical office application of FTC guidance.
sources.quote: in a locked room or in a locked file cabinet. Limit access to employees with a legitimate business need.

sources.claim: Files and final checklist: shared drives vs individual ownership, persistence after departure/account deletion, default member visibility and limited-access folders. Suggested permission review applies these documented distinctions.
sources.quote:
Your organization owns the files in a shared drive, not an individual.
limited-access folders in shared drives to control who can see the content

sources.claim: Required scripture callout: Colossians 3:23, checked on publisher reader one verse at a time. Quoted without footnote marks, retaining punctuation.
sources.publisher: The Lockman Foundation / Three Sixteen Publishing
sources.quote: Whatever you do, do your work heartily, as for the Lord rather than for men,

claim_check.notes: Author researched sources and checked scripture; independent Opus review of claims, verse and desktop/mobile screenshots remains pending. Section-level source claims map factual prose and practical applications. Volatile services checked 2026-10-16.

rulings: Use Google as a feature example only, without endorsement, prices, quotas or eligibility promises.
Present OSHA and FTC material as practical setup guidance, not a conclusion about church-specific legal coverage.
Keep legal address, renewal timing, retention schedules, purchasing policy and pastoral methodology outside this guide.
Practical checklists apply the cited source features; they are not additional legal requirements.
